- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is low or neutral (sentiment < 0.27).  
- Underestimate downward corrections after high peaks; model tends to lag in recognizing sharp drops.  
- When sentiment is consistently low (last 3–5 days < 0.18), reduce forecasted mean by 1–2% to account for bearish bias.  
- After a 3–5 day run of rising prices, model overreacts to short-term volatility; cap forecasted peaks at 10–15% below recent high.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion within 7–10 days, adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of history.  
- When sentiment is high (last 3 days > 0.44), model tends to overpredict continuation; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5 days.
